---
title: "State of health in BC: a descriptive report"
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Version and observation window

**Report version 0.5** · observation windows: mortality **1991–2024**,
life expectancy **1980–2024**, survey indicators **2015–2024**,
sub-provincial mortality **2020/2023**, sub-provincial life expectancy
**2006–2017**, sub-provincial survey **2015/2016–2023/2024** · generated
from the published datasets by `quarto render`. Regenerate the underlying
data with `uv run sohbc build` before re-rendering (see
[Reproduce](#reproduce)).

Numbers in this report are **regenerated on every build** from the files
under `data/published/`; nothing here is typed in by hand. If a figure and
this prose disagree, the figure is right.
:::

This is an edition of the project's "State of health in BC" descriptive
report (deliverable of milestone M3 in the [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md)). It
describes what the currently-ingested indicators show — **not** the state
of health in full. The indicator set now spans mortality and survey-based
morbidity, mental health, and wellbeing, and reaches **below the province**
to regional mortality, life expectancy, and survey gaps; the report will
keep widening, and each edition carries its observation window because the
numbers are dated, not timeless ([why](../explanation/nonstationarity.qmd)).

## What is covered

| Indicator | Domain | Window | Resolution | Sexes | Source |
|-----------|--------|--------|------------|-------|--------|
| [Mortality rates](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd) | Mortality | 1991–2024 | provincial | both, M, F; 20 age groups | StatCan 13-10-0710-01 |
| [Life expectancy at birth](indicator-life-expectancy-bc.qmd) | Mortality | 1980–2024 | provincial | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0837-01 |
| [Regional mortality inequality](indicator-mortality-inequality-bc.qmd) | Mortality | 2020/2023 | health authority, HSDA | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0931-01 |
| [Regional life expectancy](indicator-life-expectancy-regions-bc.qmd) | Mortality | 2006/2008–2015/2017 | health authority, HSDA | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0389-01 |
| [Life satisfaction](indicator-life-satisfaction-bc.qmd) | Subjective wellbeing | 2015–2024 | provincial | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0905-01 |
| [Ten survey indicators](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd) | Morbidity, mental health, wellbeing, access to care | 2015–2024 | provincial | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0905-01 |
| [Survey indicators across regions](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd#the-regional-view) | Morbidity, mental health, wellbeing | 2015/2016–2023/2024 | HSDA | both, M, F | StatCan 13-10-0972-01 |

All are **proxies** for their domains, not the state of health itself. Four
indicators now reach sub-provincial resolution; the rest remain
provincial (see [Next editions](#next-editions)).

## The headline: every series moves, and the rules change

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mort = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_rates_bc_trend.json").json()
mortAsr = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_rates_bc_age_standardised_trend.json").json()
life = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc_trend.json").json()
lifeBySex = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc_by_sex_trend.json").json()
mortBySex = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_rates_bc_by_sex_trend.json").json()

surveyKeys = [
  ["Life satisfaction", "life_satisfaction_bc"],
  ["Perceived health, fair or poor", "perceived_health_fair_poor_bc"],
  ["Perceived mental health, fair or poor", "perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc"],
  ["Sense of belonging", "sense_of_belonging_bc"],
  ["Anxiety disorder", "anxiety_disorder_bc"],
  ["Mood disorder", "mood_disorder_bc"],
  ["Diabetes", "diabetes_bc"],
  ["High blood pressure", "high_blood_pressure_bc"],
  ["Has a regular provider", "has_regular_provider_bc"],
  ["Daily smoker", "smoker_daily_bc"]
]
tLifeSat = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_trend.json").json()
tPhyH = await FileAttachment("../data/published/perceived_health_fair_poor_bc_trend.json").json()
tMentH = await FileAttachment("../data/published/perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc_trend.json").json()
tBelong = await FileAttachment("../data/published/sense_of_belonging_bc_trend.json").json()
tAnx = await FileAttachment("../data/published/anxiety_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tMood = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mood_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tDiab = await FileAttachment("../data/published/diabetes_bc_trend.json").json()
tBp = await FileAttachment("../data/published/high_blood_pressure_bc_trend.json").json()
tProv = await FileAttachment("../data/published/has_regular_provider_bc_trend.json").json()
tSmoke = await FileAttachment("../data/published/smoker_daily_bc_trend.json").json()
survey = [
  {label: "Life satisfaction", t: tLifeSat},
  {label: "Perceived health, fair or poor", t: tPhyH},
  {label: "Perceived mental health, fair or poor", t: tMentH},
  {label: "Sense of belonging", t: tBelong},
  {label: "Anxiety disorder", t: tAnx},
  {label: "Mood disorder", t: tMood},
  {label: "Diabetes", t: tDiab},
  {label: "High blood pressure", t: tBp},
  {label: "Has a regular provider", t: tProv},
  {label: "Daily smoker", t: tSmoke}
]

summary = [
  {series: "Mortality rate (crude)", window: `${mort.start}–${mort.end}`, slope_per_decade: mort.overall.slope_per_decade, verdict: mort.stationarity.verdict, breaks: mort.change_points.join(", ") || "—"},
  {series: "Mortality rate (age-standardised)", window: `${mortAsr.start}–${mortAsr.end}`, slope_per_decade: mortAsr.overall.slope_per_decade, verdict: mortAsr.stationarity.verdict, breaks: mortAsr.change_points.join(", ") || "—"},
  {series: "Life expectancy at birth", window: `${life.start}–${life.end}`, slope_per_decade: life.overall.slope_per_decade, verdict: life.stationarity.verdict, breaks: life.change_points.join(", ") || "—"},
  ...survey.map(s => ({series: s.label, window: `${s.t.start}–${s.t.end}`, slope_per_decade: s.t.overall.slope_per_decade, verdict: s.t.stationarity.verdict, breaks: s.t.change_points.join(", ") || "—"}))
]
Inputs.table(summary, {
  columns: ["series", "window", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "breaks"],
  header: {series: "series", window: "window", slope_per_decade: "slope/decade", verdict: "stationarity", breaks: "regime breaks"}
})
```

Several things follow from the table, and they are the report's core
finding:

1. **Almost nothing is stationary.** Nearly every series changes over its
   window; a single summary value would be false to almost all of them.
   Two — diabetes and having a regular provider — are labelled stationary
   over their short window, so absence of evidence is reported as such.
2. **Direction differs by measure.** The crude mortality rate and life
   expectancy trend in opposite senses, because crude mortality is not
   age-adjusted while life expectancy already integrates the age pattern
   of death; the survey series likewise split, with wellbeing falling
   while self-reported poor health and mental-health conditions rise.
3. **The change is not one slope.** Many series carry a regime break
   beyond a straight line, several dated to 2020; the breaks are the
   story, not noise.

## Regimes are slope changes, not level shifts

A regime break can mean two different things: the series **steps** to a new
level, or it keeps its level but changes its **rate** of movement. The
pipeline now separates the two, and for almost every indicator it is the
second.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
decomp = [
  {series: "Mortality rate (crude)", d: mort},
  {series: "Life expectancy at birth", d: life},
  {series: "Life satisfaction", d: tLifeSat},
  {series: "Sense of belonging", d: tBelong},
  {series: "Anxiety disorder", d: tAnx},
  {series: "Mood disorder", d: tMood},
  {series: "Perceived mental health, fair or poor", d: tMentH},
  {series: "Perceived health, fair or poor", d: tPhyH},
  {series: "Daily smoker", d: tSmoke},
  {series: "High blood pressure", d: tBp},
  {series: "Diabetes", d: tDiab},
  {series: "Has a regular provider", d: tProv}
].map(({series, d}) => {
  const dc = d.decomposition || {}
  const jumps = d.jumps || []
  const segs = d.segments || []
  // Within-regime rates in points per decade, side by side, so a
  // slope-change break reads as "the pace changed", not "the level moved".
  const regimeRates = segs.map(g => `${g.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)} (${g.start}–${g.end})`)
  const tests = d.slope_change_tests || []
  const slopeTest = tests.length
    ? tests.map(t => `${t.change_point}: ${t.significant ? "yes" : "no"} (p=${t.p_value.toFixed(3)})`).join("; ")
    : "—"
  return {
    series,
    observed: dc.observed_change ?? "—",
    within: dc.within_regime_change ?? "—",
    between: dc.between_regime_change ?? "—",
    share_between: dc.observed_change
      ? Math.abs(dc.between_regime_change) / (Math.abs(dc.within_regime_change) + Math.abs(dc.between_regime_change))
      : 0,
    regimes: regimeRates.length > 1 ? regimeRates.join(" → ") : "single regime",
    slope_change: slopeTest,
    jumps: jumps.map(j => `${j.year}: ${j.jump.toFixed(2)}`).join("; ") || "—"
  }
})
Inputs.table(decomp, {
  columns: ["series", "observed", "within", "between", "regimes", "slope_change", "jumps"],
  header: {
    series: "series", observed: "total change", within: "within-regime",
    between: "between-regime (jumps)", regimes: "within-regime rate/decade",
    slope_change: "slope-change F-test", jumps: "jumps (year: level shift)"
  },
  width: {regimes: 200, slope_change: 200, jumps: 150}
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tested = decomp.filter(d => d.slope_change !== "—")
allSig = tested.every(d => !d.slope_change.includes("no ("))
md`The "between-regime" column is nearly zero for all but one series. The
largest level shift anywhere is life expectancy at 2015
(**${life.jumps[0].jump.toFixed(2)}** years), and even there the bulk of the
change is within-regime (${life.decomposition.within_regime_change.toFixed(2)}
of ${life.decomposition.observed_change.toFixed(2)}). For the survey series
the jumps are fractions of a point. The **within-regime rate** column makes
the point directly, and the **slope-change F-test** confirms it: at every
dated break the two regimes' slopes differ significantly
(${allSig ? "all" : "most"} p < 0.05). So when this report says a series'
"rules change", it means the slope changes — the pace and direction of
movement turn, while the series does not lurch discontinuously to a new
level. That is the more common and more policy-relevant kind of
nonstationarity.`
```

## Mortality: an ageing population masks a turning point

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_rates_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
rates = rows.filter(d => d.characteristic === "Mortality rate per 1,000 population" && d.age_group === "Age at time of death, all ages" && d.sex === "Both sexes")
asr = (await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_rates_bc_age_standardised.csv").csv({typed: true})).filter(d => d.sex === "Both sexes")
series = rates.map(d => ({year: d.ref_date, rate: d.value, series: "Crude"}))
  .concat(asr.map(d => ({year: d.ref_date, rate: d.value, series: "Age-standardised"})))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  title: "Mortality rate, British Columbia (per 1,000 population)",
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {grid: true, label: "Deaths per 1,000 population"},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectX([{x1: 2020, x2: 2024}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "grey", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
    Plot.ruleX(mort.change_points, {stroke: "red", strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
    Plot.ruleX(mortAsr.change_points, {stroke: "steelblue", strokeDasharray: "2,3"}),
    Plot.lineY(series, {x: "year", y: "rate", stroke: "series", tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(series, {x: "year", y: "rate", stroke: "series", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Over ${mort.start}–${mort.end} the **crude** rate rose by
**${mort.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** per 1,000 per decade, while the
**age-standardised** rate, which removes the effect of population ageing,
changed by **${mortAsr.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** — i.e. it *fell*
on net. The crude rise is largely the ageing of the population, not a
worsening of age-specific risk. The age-standardised series is the one that
abstracts from that: it declined from 1991 and its regime turned at
**${mortAsr.change_point}**, after which the decline flattened and
reversed. The pink band marks the COVID-19 period (2020–2024).`
```

The gap between the two lines is the signature of demographic ageing, and
it is exactly why the project reports both and treats the standardised
series as the one about risk rather than the one about the age structure.
The age breakdown makes the mechanism explicit: the decline is real at
**every** age, but it scales with age (about **9.7** per 1,000 per decade
at 90 and over against **0.00** at 30–34), so a rising all-ages crude rate
coexists with falling rates at every age. The full breakdown is on the
[mortality indicator page](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd#age-breakdown).

## Life expectancy: two decades of gain, then a stall

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
lifeRows = (await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})).filter(d => d.characteristic === "Life expectancy (in years) at age x (ex)" && d.age_group === "0 years" && d.sex !== "Both sexes")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  title: "Life expectancy at birth by sex, British Columbia (years)",
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {grid: true, label: "Years", domain: [70, 90]},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectX([{x1: 2020, x2: 2024}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "grey", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
    Plot.ruleX(lifeBySex.levels.Males.change_points, {stroke: "red", strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
    Plot.ruleX(lifeBySex.levels.Females.change_points, {stroke: "steelblue", strokeDasharray: "2,3"}),
    Plot.lineY(lifeRows, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(lifeRows, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Life expectancy at birth (both sexes) rose by
**${life.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** years per decade on average
across ${life.start}–${life.end}, but as two regimes: gains of about
**${life.segments[0].slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** years per decade to
**${life.change_point}**, then a flat-to-declining
**${life.segments[1].slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** years per decade after.
The post-2015 stall spans the COVID-19 period, which is visible as the
2020–2022 dip, but the regime turn **precedes** the pandemic — the pipeline
dates the change and does not attribute it.`
```

This is the project's nonstationarity claim in one series: the same
indicator, the same source, but a different rule before and after 2015.
The male and female series turn differently (below), so even this
agreement about *whether* there was a break comes with disagreement about
*when*.

## Beyond mortality: wellbeing down, distress up

The survey family widens the report past death. Over 2015–2024, the
wellbeing series fall and the self-reported distress series rise, and
several breaks land on 2020.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cLifeSat = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
cBelong = await FileAttachment("../data/published/sense_of_belonging_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
cMentH = await FileAttachment("../data/published/perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
cAnx = await FileAttachment("../data/published/anxiety_disorder_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
cMood = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mood_disorder_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
cSmoke = await FileAttachment("../data/published/smoker_daily_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
surveyChart = [
  ["Life satisfaction", cLifeSat],
  ["Sense of belonging", cBelong],
  ["Perceived mental health, fair or poor", cMentH],
  ["Anxiety disorder", cAnx],
  ["Mood disorder", cMood],
  ["Daily smoker", cSmoke]
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
flat = surveyChart.flatMap(([series, rows]) =>
  rows.filter(d => d.sex === "Both sexes").map(d => ({year: d.ref_date, value: d.value, series}))
)
Plot.plot({
  title: "Selected survey indicators, British Columbia (% of adults)",
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {grid: true, label: "% of adults aged 18+"},
  color: {legend: false},
  facet: {data: flat, y: "series", label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectX([{x1: 2020, x2: 2024}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "grey", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
    Plot.lineY(flat, {x: "year", y: "value", stroke: "series", tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(flat, {x: "year", y: "value", stroke: "series", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ls = survey.find(s => s.label === "Life satisfaction").t
sb = survey.find(s => s.label === "Sense of belonging").t
pmh = survey.find(s => s.label === "Perceived mental health, fair or poor").t
anx = survey.find(s => s.label === "Anxiety disorder").t
moodTrend = survey.find(s => s.label === "Mood disorder").t
smk = survey.find(s => s.label === "Daily smoker").t
md`Over ${ls.start}–${ls.end} life satisfaction fell
**${ls.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}** points per decade and sense
of belonging **${sb.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**; both break at
**${ls.change_point}**. In the same window, perceived *poor* mental health
rose **${pmh.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**, anxiety disorder
**${anx.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**, and mood disorder
**${moodTrend.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}** points per decade (mood
disorder also breaks at **${moodTrend.change_point}**). Daily smoking *fell*
**${smk.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**, but its regimes split at
2020 too: **${smk.segments[0].slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**/decade before,
**${smk.segments[1].slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}**/decade after. All are
survey estimates: the 2020 coincidence is dated, not attributed, and part
of any step may be measurement (see the
[indicator family page](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd)).`
```

The survey window is short (ten annual points), so the stationarity test
has limited power and two series come back **undetermined** rather than
stationary. The family is read side by side on the
[indicator family page](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd).

## Sex differences

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sexRows = ["Males", "Females"].flatMap(sex => [
  {indicator: "Life expectancy", sex, ...lifeBySex.levels[sex]},
  {indicator: "Mortality (crude)", sex, ...mortBySex.crude[sex]},
  {indicator: "Mortality (age-standardised)", sex, ...mortBySex.age_standardised[sex]}
]).map(d => ({
  indicator: d.indicator,
  sex: d.sex,
  window: `${d.start}–${d.end}`,
  slope_per_decade: d.overall.slope_per_decade,
  verdict: d.stationarity.verdict,
  breaks: d.change_points.join(", ") || "—"
}))
Inputs.table(sexRows, {
  columns: ["indicator", "sex", "window", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "breaks"],
  header: {indicator: "indicator", sex: "sex", window: "window", slope_per_decade: "slope/decade", verdict: "stationarity", breaks: "regime breaks"}
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
lifeFull = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
finalYear = lifeBySex.levels.Females.end
finalFemale = lifeFull.find(d => Number(d.ref_date) === finalYear && d.age_group === "0 years" && d.sex === "Females" && d.characteristic === "Life expectancy (in years) at age x (ex)").value
finalMale = lifeFull.find(d => Number(d.ref_date) === finalYear && d.age_group === "0 years" && d.sex === "Males" && d.characteristic === "Life expectancy (in years) at age x (ex)").value
md`In ${finalYear}, life expectancy at birth was **${finalFemale.toFixed(1)}**
years for females versus **${finalMale.toFixed(1)}** for males, a gap of
about ${(finalFemale - finalMale).toFixed(1)} years. Both sexes moved in
regimes rather than one straight line: the male series turns at
**${lifeBySex.levels.Males.change_point}** and the female at
**${lifeBySex.levels.Females.change_point}**, so a single both-sexes
trajectory would blur two differently-timed changes. On the
age-standardised mortality series the male decline-then-reversal is
steeper than the female (males' regime breaks at
${mortBySex.age_standardised.Males.change_point}, females' at
${mortBySex.age_standardised.Females.change_point}).`
```

## Inequalities across regions

The sub-provincial view is published for mortality, life expectancy, and
the survey family. The newest of the three, using Statistics Canada table
13-10-0931-01 (three-year averages, 2021/2023), shows the age-standardised
premature-mortality rate varying widely across BC's health service
delivery areas.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
disp = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mortality_inequality_bc_dispersion.json").json()
prem = disp.dispersion["Premature mortality"]["Both sexes"]
avoid = disp.dispersion["Potentially avoidable mortality"]["Both sexes"]
regions = prem.regions.map(r => ({region: r.region.replace(" Health Service Delivery Area", ""), value: r.value}))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  title: `Age-standardised premature mortality by health service delivery area, ${prem.ref_date} (per 100,000)`,
  marginLeft: 170,
  x: {grid: true, label: "Premature deaths per 100,000"},
  y: {label: null, domain: regions.map(d => d.region)},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(regions, {y: "region", x: "value", fill: "value", tip: true}),
    Plot.ruleX([prem.mean], {stroke: "black", strokeDasharray: "4,4"})
  ],
  color: {scheme: "Reds", legend: false}
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Across **${prem.n_regions}** health service delivery areas, premature
mortality ranges from **${prem.lowest.value.toFixed(1)}** in
${prem.lowest.region.replace(" Health Service Delivery Area", "")} to
**${prem.highest.value.toFixed(1)}** in
${prem.highest.region.replace(" Health Service Delivery Area", "")} — a
**${prem.ratio.toFixed(1)}×** gap, against a provincial average of about
${prem.mean.toFixed(0)}. Potentially avoidable mortality shows the same
pattern (${avoid.ratio.toFixed(1)}×). The dashed line is the mean across
areas. The northern and interior service delivery areas are consistently
highest, the Vancouver-metro areas lowest.`
```

This is a genuine inequality signal, and it is exactly what a
provincial-average report hides. Two limits apply. First, the source is
**three-year averages** and covers only two overlapping periods, so it
supports this cross-sectional snapshot but **not** a regional trajectory —
the trend machinery is not run on it. Second, the rate confidence
intervals overlap between neighbouring regions, so the ordering at the
middle of the distribution is not sharp; the roughly 3× gap between the
extremes is. **No causal claim** is made here: the regional pattern
co-moves with age structure, remoteness, and service access, which are
M4/M5 questions.

### Life expectancy across regions

The sub-provincial view now extends to life expectancy
([indicator page](indicator-life-expectancy-regions-bc.qmd)). The only
published source, table 13-10-0389-01, ends at 2015/2017 on 2018
boundaries — a pre-pandemic baseline, not the current picture.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
leReg = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc_regions_summary.json").json()
leBirth = leReg.series.find(s => s.age_group === "At birth")
leLatest = leReg.reference_periods[leReg.reference_periods.length - 1]
leSpread = leBirth.spread.health_authority[leLatest]
leProv = leBirth.trajectories.province["British Columbia"]
leShort = n => n.replace(" Health Authority", "")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
leRows = leSpread.regions.map(r => ({region: leShort(r.region), value: r.value}))
Plot.plot({
  title: `Life expectancy at birth by health authority, ${leLatest} (years)`,
  marginLeft: 130,
  x: {grid: true, label: "Years"},
  y: {label: null, domain: leRows.map(d => d.region)},
  marks: [Plot.barX(leRows, {y: "region", x: "value", fill: "value", tip: true})],
  color: {scheme: "Teals", legend: false}
})
```

### Survey indicators across regions

The survey family also has a regional view
([indicator page](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd#the-regional-view)),
from table 13-10-0972-01: the same nine measures across BC's 16 health
service delivery areas, as five pooled two-year periods over 2015–2024.
The regional gap is wide — daily smoking varies about **3×** across
areas, diabetes **2.5×** — and areas do not rank the same way on every
series. With five pooled periods per area the stationarity verdict is
*undetermined* throughout, so this view reports levels and gaps, not
dated regional regimes. Together with the mortality-inequality view, the
report no longer speaks of one BC: the regional spread is real, it
differs by domain, and a provincial average is a summary of unequal
parts.

## Reading this report

- **Dates are the point.** Every number above belongs to its window;
  reproducing the pipeline on refreshed data may change the verdicts.
- **Proxies, several domains.** Mortality and life expectancy are
  mortality-domain proxies; the survey family adds self-reported
  morbidity, mental health, wellbeing, and access to care. None is the
  state of health itself, and a self-report is not a diagnosis.
- **Break detection is not explanation.** The dated regimes come from a
  formal test of departure from a straight line
  [@truong2020selective]; the test says *where* the rule changes, not
  *why*. The within-versus-across split is backed by a Chow-style F-test
  of equal slopes either side of each break [@chow1960], which says the
  *pace* changed, not just the level. Attribution is M4/M5 work.
- **Aggregates hide sub-series.** A both-sexes series is not a summary of
  the male and female trajectories; read them separately.
- **Survey versus administrative.** The mortality series are
  administrative (complete counts), the survey series are samples: the
  latter carry sampling error, suppression, and a mid-series collection
  change, so a survey step may be measurement, not change.
- **Resolution comes with its own limits.** A sub-provincial number is
  not a better provincial one: the regional series are pooled averages on
  their own boundary vintages, so they date differently and never pool
  with the provincial series or with each other across boundary sets.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run sohbc fetch statcan_wds statcan_life_tables statcan_health_indicators statcan_health_regions statcan_life_tables_regions statcan_health_regions_cchs
uv run sohbc build
quarto render reference/state-of-health-report.qmd
```

The report reads only the files under `data/published/`, so it regenerates
end-to-end from raw data with the commands above — the acceptance
criterion of milestone M3.
